newsitem.title: FRANCE: Soc Gen, BNP, CIC cut French base rates to 6.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Soc Gen, BNP, CIC cut French base rates to 6.3 pct.

text.p: Several French banks announced on Monday that they were reducing their base lending rates to 6.30 percent from 6.55 percent in a move that could help boost France's sluggish economy.
Two of France's biggest mainstream banks, Societe Generale and Banque Nationale de Paris, along with regional banking group CIC said that they were reducing their base rates.

Specialised property lender Credit Commercial de France also announced it was cutting its base rate to 6.30 percent from 6.55 percent. The banks last cut their base rates at which they lend to their best customers on September 20.
The centre-right government has been urging commercial banks to pass on interest rate cuts by the country's central bank, the Bank of France.

The Bank left its interest rates unchanged earlier on Monday at its twice-weekly money market tender, but economists saw further easing in the months ahead in wake of European Union accord on a post monetary union budget discipline pact reached on the weekend.
